Probability and Statistics

Descriptive Statistics

Population, Sample, and Percentiles

Def. (Population, Parameter, Statistic)

Population: the entire group under consideration.

Parameter: a numerical measure depending on all units in the population; a characteristic of the population.

Statistic: a numerical measure depending only on the sampled units; a characteristic of the sample.

Def. (Population Percentiles / Quantiles)

The 100p100p100pth percentile is the location that indicates the percent of a distribution equal to or below 100p100p100p.

First quartile Q1Q_1Q1​: p=0.25p=0.25p=0.25; median Q2Q_2Q2​: p=0.5p=0.5p=0.5; third quartile Q3Q_3Q3​: p=0.75p=0.75p=0.75.

Interquartile range (IQR): Q3−Q1Q_3-Q_1Q3​−Q1​.

The sample median is more robust to outliers than the sample mean. If the sample is sorted as x(1)≤⋯≤x(n)x_{(1)}\le \cdots\le x_{(n)}x(1)​≤⋯≤x(n)​: - Odd nnn: sample median is the value at position (n+1)/2(n+1)/2(n+1)/2. - Even nnn: sample median is the average of values at positions n/2n/2n/2 and n/2+1n/2+1n/2+1.

Def. (Sample 100p100p100pth Percentile)

The sample 100p100p100pth percentile x~\tilde{x}x~ of a dataset is a value with at least npnpnp observations ≤x~\le\tilde{x}≤x~ and at least n(1−p)n(1-p)n(1−p) observations ≥x~\ge\tilde{x}≥x~.

If npnpnp is not an integer, use the next integer greater than npnpnp. If npnpnp is an integer, use the average of the values in the corresponding two positions.

Shape of a Distribution

- Unimodal, symmetric bell-shaped distribution: mean ≈\approx≈ median. - Unimodal distribution skewed to the left: mean <<< median.

Sample Space, Events, and Axioms

Def. (Sample Space and Event)

The sample space SSS of an experiment is the set of all possible outcomes of the experiment.

An event E⊆SE\subseteq SE⊆S occurs if the outcome of the experiment belongs to EEE.

Conditional Probability and Bayes' Formula

Def. (Conditional Probability)

The probability of event EEE given that event FFF has occurred:

P(E∣F)=P(E∩F)P(F),P(F)>0.P(E\mid F)=\frac{P(E\cap F)}{P(F)},\qquad P(F)>0.P(E∣F)=P(F)P(E∩F)​,P(F)>0.

Thm. (Bayes' Formula)

For mutually exclusive and exhaustive events F1,…,FnF_1,\ldots,F_nF1​,…,Fn​,

P(Fi∣E)=P(E∣Fi)P(Fi)∑j=1nP(E∣Fj)P(Fj).P(F_i\mid E)=\frac{P(E\mid F_i)P(F_i)}{\sum_{j=1}^nP(E\mid F_j)P(F_j)}.P(Fi​∣E)=∑j=1n​P(E∣Fj​)P(Fj​)P(E∣Fi​)P(Fi​)​.

Also P(E∣F)=P(F∣E)P(E)/P(F)P(E\mid F)=P(F\mid E)P(E)/P(F)P(E∣F)=P(F∣E)P(E)/P(F) after rearrangement.

Def. (Independent Events)

EEE and FFF are independent if P(E∩F)=P(E)P(F)P(E\cap F)=P(E)P(F)P(E∩F)=P(E)P(F).

Prop. (Independence)

  1. If EEE and FFF are independent, so are EEE and FcF^cFc.

P(E)=P(E∩F)+P(E∩Fc)=P(E)P(F)+P(E∩Fc).P(E)=P(E\cap F)+P(E\cap F^c) =P(E)P(F)+P(E\cap F^c).P(E)=P(E∩F)+P(E∩Fc)=P(E)P(F)+P(E∩Fc).

Let X1,…,XnX_1,\ldots,X_nX1​,…,Xn​ be independent and identically distributed random variables with mean μ\muμ and variance σ2\sigma^2σ2. Then for every ε>0\varepsilon>0ε>0,

Hypothesis Testing

Null Hypothesis, Alternative, and Errors

Def. (Statistical Hypotheses)

The null hypothesis H0H_0H0​ is what is to be tested, usually the negation of the assertion or effect under examination.

The alternative hypothesis H1H_1H1​ is the competing assertion.

A statistical test is a procedure for choosing whether to reject H0H_0H0​.

Hypotheses are expressed using population parameters, not sample statistics (which are observed quantities).

Def. (Critical / Rejection Region)

A critical (rejection) region CCC is a set of observations or test statistic values for which H0H_0H0​ is rejected.

Failure to reject H0H_0H0​ does not mean H0H_0H0​ is true; only that the data did not provide sufficient evidence against it.

Decision / Actual H0H_0H0​ true H1H_1H1​ true
Reject H0H_0H0​ Type I error (α\alphaα) Correct rejection
Fail to reject H0H_0H0​ Correct decision Type II error (β\betaβ)

Def. (Type I / II Error, Power, Significance)

Type I error (α)(\alpha)(α): rejecting H0H_0H0​ when it is true.

Type II error (β)(\beta)(β): failing to reject H0H_0H0​ when it is false.

Power: P(reject H0∣H1 true)=1−βP(\text{reject }H_0\mid H_1\text{ true})=1-\betaP(reject H0​∣H1​ true)=1−β.

Significance level α\alphaα: under H0H_0H0​, P(reject H0)≤αP(\text{reject }H_0)\le\alphaP(reject H0​)≤α.

General steps of a test: 1. State H0,H1H_0,H_1H0​,H1​ (population parameters). 2. Set significance level α\alphaα. 3. Fix test statistic (point estimator / test statistic). 4. Determine the critical region CCC and collect data. 5. Evaluate the test statistic. 6. Decide to reject or fail to reject H0H_0H0​ at α\alphaα. 7. Interpret the decision.

Tests for a Normal Mean, Known Variance

For a normal random sample X1,…,Xn∼N(μ,σ2)X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)X1​,…,Xn​∼N(μ,σ2), σ\sigmaσ known,

Z=X‾−μ0σ/n∼N(0,1)under H0:μ=μ0.Z=\frac{\overline X-\mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt n} \sim N(0,1)\quad\text{under }H_0:\mu=\mu_0.Z=σ/n​X−μ0​​∼N(0,1)under H0​:μ=μ0​.

Thm. (One-Sided Z Test)

For H0:μ≤μ0H_0:\mu\le\mu_0H0​:μ≤μ0​ versus H1:μ>μ0H_1:\mu>\mu_0H1​:μ>μ0​:

Reject H0ifX‾−μ0σ/n>zα.\text{Reject }H_0\quad\text{if}\quad \frac{\overline X-\mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt n}>z_\alpha.Reject H0​ifσ/n​X−μ0​​>zα​.

For H0:μ≥μ0H_0:\mu\ge\mu_0H0​:μ≥μ0​ versus H1:μ<μ0H_1:\mu<\mu_0H1​:μ<μ0​:

Reject H0ifZ<−zα.\text{Reject }H_0\quad\text{if}\quad Z<-z_\alpha.Reject H0​ifZ<−zα​.

Thm. (Two-Sided Z Test)

For H0:μ=μ0H_0:\mu=\mu_0H0​:μ=μ0​ versus H1:μ≠μ0H_1:\mu\ne\mu_0H1​:μ=μ0​,

Reject H0if∣Z∣>zα/2.\text{Reject }H_0\quad\text{if}\quad |Z|>z_{\alpha/2}.Reject H0​if∣Z∣>zα/2​.

Otherwise fail to reject H0H_0H0​.

Def. (p-value)

The p-value is the smallest significance level at which the given data lead to rejection of H0H_0H0​.

If p-value <α<\alpha<α, reject H0H_0H0​.

If p-value ≥α\ge\alpha≥α, fail to reject H0H_0H0​.

For right-tailed Z=zZ=zZ=z: p=P(Z≥z)p=P(Z\ge z)p=P(Z≥z).

For two-sided Z=zZ=zZ=z: p=P(∣Z∣≥∣z∣)p=P(|Z|\ge|z|)p=P(∣Z∣≥∣z∣).

Def. (Simple Linear Regression Model)

SSW=∑i∑j(Xij−Xˉi⋅)2=∑i(n−1)Si2,SS_W=\sum_i\sum_j(X_{ij}-\bar X_{i\cdot})^2 =\sum_i(n-1)S_i^2,SSW​=i∑​j∑​(Xij​−Xˉi⋅​)2=i∑​(n−1)Si2​,

where Si2S_i^2Si2​ is the sample variance of the iiith group. When H0H_0H0​ is true,

SSBσ2∼χm−12,E[SSBm−1]=σ2.\frac{SS_B}{\sigma^2}\sim\chi^2_{m-1},\quad E\left[\frac{SS_B}{m-1}\right]=\sigma^2.σ2SSB​​∼χm−12​,E[m−1SSB​​]=σ2.

Thm. (One-Way ANOVA F Test)

F=SSB/(m−1)SSW/[m(n−1)]∼Fm−1,m(n−1)(H0).F=\frac{SS_B/(m-1)}{SS_W/[m(n-1)]} \sim F_{m-1,m(n-1)}\qquad(H_0).F=SSW​/[m(n−1)]SSB​/(m−1)​∼Fm−1,m(n−1)​(H0​).

Reject H0H_0H0​ for sufficiently large FFF:

F>Fα,m−1,m(n−1).F>F_{\alpha,m-1,m(n-1)}.F>Fα,m−1,m(n−1)​.

Multiple Comparisons of Sample Means

When H0H_0H0​ of equal means is rejected, we are interested in a comparison of different sample means μ1,…,μm\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_mμ1​,…,μm​. There are (m2)\binom m2(2m​) simultaneous tests: H0:μ1=μ2H_0:\mu_1=\mu_2H0​:μ1​=μ2​, …, H0:μm−1=μmH_0:\mu_{m-1}=\mu_mH0​:μm−1​=μm​. Ex. m=3m=3m=3: test H0:μ1=μ2H_0:\mu_1=\mu_2H0​:μ1​=μ2​, H0:μ2=μ3H_0:\mu_2=\mu_3H0​:μ2​=μ3​, H0:μ1=μ3H_0:\mu_1=\mu_3H0​:μ1​=μ3​. Assume that we conduct two independent tests. αe\alpha_eαe​: overall type I error. αIi\alpha_{I_i}αIi​​: individual type I error of test iii.

αe=P(falsely reject test 1 or 2)=1−P(correctly not reject both tests)\alpha_e=P(\text{falsely reject test 1 or 2}) =1-P(\text{correctly not reject both tests})αe​=P(falsely reject test 1 or 2)=1−P(correctly not reject both tests)

=1−P(correctly not reject test 1)P(correctly not reject test 2)=1-P(\text{correctly not reject test 1})P(\text{correctly not reject test 2})=1−P(correctly not reject test 1)P(correctly not reject test 2)

=1−[1−P(αI1)][1−P(αI2)].=1-[1-P(\alpha_{I_1})][1-P(\alpha_{I_2})].=1−[1−P(αI1​​)][1−P(αI2​​)].

Let αI1=αI2=0.05\alpha_{I_1}=\alpha_{I_2}=0.05αI1​​=αI2​​=0.05, then αe≈0.0975\alpha_e\approx0.0975αe​≈0.0975. 3 tests: αe≈0.143\alpha_e\approx0.143αe​≈0.143. 4 tests: the overall error increases further.

ANOVA with Unequal Sample Sizes

Let group iii contain nin_ini​ observations, i=1,…,mi=1,\ldots,mi=1,…,m, and total N=∑iniN=\sum_i n_iN=∑i​ni​.

Def. (ANOVA Sums of Squares: Unequal Sizes)

SSW=∑i=1m∑j=1ni(Xij−X‾i⋅)2,SS_W=\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}(X_{ij}-\overline X_{i\cdot})^2,SSW​=i=1∑m​j=1∑ni​​(Xij​−Xi⋅​)2,

X‾⋅⋅=1N∑iniX‾i⋅,SSB=∑i=1mni(X‾i⋅−X‾⋅⋅)2.\overline X_{\cdot\cdot}=\frac1N\sum_i n_i\overline X_{i\cdot}, \qquad SS_B=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i(\overline X_{i\cdot}-\overline X_{\cdot\cdot})^2.X⋅⋅​=N1​i∑​ni​Xi⋅​,SSB​=i=1∑m​ni​(Xi⋅​−X⋅⋅​)2.

For equal population variances,

SSWσ2∼χN−m2,SSBσ2∼χm−12under H0.\frac{SS_W}{\sigma^2}\sim\chi^2_{N-m}, \qquad \frac{SS_B}{\sigma^2}\sim\chi^2_{m-1}\quad\text{under }H_0.σ2SSW​​∼χN−m2​,σ2SSB​​∼χm−12​under H0​.

Thm. (ANOVA F Test: Unequal Sample Sizes)

F=SSB/(m−1)SSW/(N−m)∼Fm−1,N−m(H0).F=\frac{SS_B/(m-1)}{SS_W/(N-m)} \sim F_{m-1,N-m}\quad(H_0).F=SSW​/(N−m)SSB​/(m−1)​∼Fm−1,N−m​(H0​).

Chi-Square Tests for Categorical Data

Goodness-of-Fit Test

Def. (Goodness-of-Fit Test)

Test whether an assumed probability mechanism or model is appropriate for observed categorical data.

For random sample Y1,…,YnY_1,\ldots,Y_nY1​,…,Yn​ taking values 1,…,k1,\ldots,k1,…,k:

H0:P(Yi=j)=pj,j=1,…,k,H_0:P(Y_i=j)=p_j,\quad j=1,\ldots,k,H0​:P(Yi​=j)=pj​,j=1,…,k,

H1:P(Yi=j)≠pjfor some j.H_1:P(Y_i=j)\ne p_j\quad\text{for some }j.H1​:P(Yi​=j)=pj​for some j.

Observed frequency XjX_jXj​ is the number of YiY_iYi​ equal to jjj; expected frequency under H0H_0H0​ is npjnp_jnpj​.

T=∑j=1k(Xj−npj)2npj.T=\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{(X_j-np_j)^2}{np_j}.T=j=1∑k​npj​(Xj​−npj​)2​.

Under H0H_0H0​, T∼approxχk−12T\overset{\rm approx}{\sim}\chi^2_{k-1}T∼approxχk−12​ for sufficiently large expected cell counts.

Prop. (Two-Category Chi-Square Statistic)

For k=2k=2k=2, X1+X2=nX_1+X_2=nX1​+X2​=n and p1+p2=1p_1+p_2=1p1​+p2​=1,

T=(X1−np1)2np1+(X2−np2)2np2T=\frac{(X_1-np_1)^2}{np_1}+ \frac{(X_2-np_2)^2}{np_2}T=np1​(X1​−np1​)2​+np2​(X2​−np2​)2​

=(X1−np1)2(1np1+1n(1−p1))=(X1−np1)2np1(1−p1).=(X_1-np_1)^2\left(\frac1{np_1}+\frac1{n(1-p_1)}\right) =\frac{(X_1-np_1)^2}{np_1(1-p_1)}.=(X1​−np1​)2(np1​1​+n(1−p1​)1​)=np1​(1−p1​)(X1​−np1​)2​.

Thus T=Z2T=Z^2T=Z2, where ZZZ is the approximate normal statistic for a single population proportion.

Tests of Independence in Contingency Tables

Suppose each unit is classified by two categorical characteristics XXX and YYY. Let XXX have categories 1,…,r1,\ldots,r1,…,r and YYY categories 1,…,c1,\ldots,c1,…,c.

Def. (Independence in a Contingency Table)

pij=P(X=i,Y=j),pi⋅=P(X=i),p⋅j=P(Y=j).p_{ij}=P(X=i,Y=j),\quad p_{i\cdot}=P(X=i),\quad p_{\cdot j}=P(Y=j).pij​=P(X=i,Y=j),pi⋅​=P(X=i),p⋅j​=P(Y=j).

Under the independence null:

H0:pij=pi⋅p⋅jfor every i,j.H_0:p_{ij}=p_{i\cdot}p_{\cdot j}\quad\text{for every }i,j.H0​:pij​=pi⋅​p⋅j​for every i,j.

H1H_1H1​: at least one pair is associated (not independent).

Counts and expected frequencies. NijN_{ij}Nij​ is the number in cell (i,j)(i,j)(i,j), and

p^i⋅=Ni⋅N,p^⋅j=N⋅jN,Eij=Np^i⋅p^⋅j=Ni⋅N⋅jN.\hat p_{i\cdot}=\frac{N_{i\cdot}}N,\quad \hat p_{\cdot j}=\frac{N_{\cdot j}}N, \quad E_{ij}=N\hat p_{i\cdot}\hat p_{\cdot j} =\frac{N_{i\cdot}N_{\cdot j}}N.p^​i⋅​=NNi⋅​​,p^​⋅j​=NN⋅j​​,Eij​=Np^​i⋅​p^​⋅j​=NNi⋅​N⋅j​​.

X\YX\backslash YX\Y 1 2 … Total
1 N11N_{11}N11​ N12N_{12}N12​ … N1⋅N_{1\cdot}N1⋅​
2 N21N_{21}N21​ N22N_{22}N22​ … N2⋅N_{2\cdot}N2⋅​
Total N⋅1N_{\cdot1}N⋅1​ N⋅2N_{\cdot2}N⋅2​ … NNN

Thm. (Chi-Square Test of Independence)

T=∑i=1r∑j=1c(Nij−Eij)2Eij∼approxχ(r−1)(c−1)2(H0).T=\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{j=1}^c \frac{(N_{ij}-E_{ij})^2}{E_{ij}} \overset{\rm approx}{\sim}\chi^2_{(r-1)(c-1)} \quad(H_0).T=i=1∑r​j=1∑c​Eij​(Nij​−Eij​)2​∼approxχ(r−1)(c−1)2​(H0​).

Reject independence for sufficiently large TTT.

For a 2×22\times22×2 table, the chi-square test corresponds asymptotically to a two-sample population proportion test.
